chunks: When you intend to enter al-Masjid al-Haram, then enter through the Gate of Banu Shaybah barefoot. Put your right foot in before the left, and maintain tranquility and dignity, for whoever enters it with humility is forgiven.

And say, while you are at the door of the mosque: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and from Allah, and as Allah has willed. Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah and his family. Peace be upon Ibrahim and his family. Peace be upon the Prophets of Allah and His messengers. And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ: a greeting of peace addressed to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds
key_terms.بَابِ بَنِي شَيْبَةَ: the Gate of Banu Shaybah, specified here as the entrance point
key_terms.حَافِيًا: barefoot, as part of the entry etiquette

ai.seo_question: What should be said and done when entering al-Masjid al-Haram?
ai.summary: This passage teaches the etiquette of entering al-Masjid al-Haram, including humility, calmness, and beginning with the right foot. It also preserves a specific du'a and greeting to be recited at the entrance, combining reverence for the sacred place with remembrance of Allah and salutations upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, Ibrahim, and the other prophets.
